findings.title: ensure_logged_in before_filter breaks the email one-click unsubscribe flow
findings.body: `:unsubscribe` is added to the `ensure_logged_in` before_filter list (line 28), so a recipient clicking the unsubscribe link delivered in an email — who by definition is not authenticated — is bounced to the login page before reaching the action. The entire purpose of the per-topic unsubscribe link is to give the user a single, friction-free way out from their mail client; forcing a login defeats that. The action either needs to be excluded from `ensure_logged_in` and instead authorised via a signed, expiring token (the RFC 8058 one-click unsubscribe pattern), or the link should not be sent to anyone who isn't already signed in. As shipped, the new email copy added in server.en.yml (`unsubscribe_link`) and the `unsubscribe_url` interpolation in user_notifications.rb route users into a flow that will not work.

findings.title: TopicUser.find_by result used without a nil check, raising NoMethodError
findings.body: `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` at line 105 may return nil — for example when the recipient has never visited the topic, when a `TopicUser` row was removed independently, or when the notification email was sent by a path that didn't go through `TopicUser.change` and so never created the row. The next two lines (`tu.notification_level > …`, `tu.notification_level = …`) and the subsequent `tu.save!` all dereference `tu` and will raise NoMethodError, surfacing a 500 instead of performing the unsubscribe. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, params[:topic_id], notification_level: …)` (which creates a row when missing), or guard `tu` against nil and respond with a redirect or 404.

findings.title: Per-topic unsubscribe is a GET with side effects, no CSRF token, and no per-user signature
findings.body: Both unsubscribe routes are defined as `get` and the controller action mutates `TopicUser#notification_level`. There is no signed token in `topic.unsubscribe_url` (it is just `#{Discourse.base_url}/t/#{slug}/#{id}/unsubscribe`, which is guessable from the topic id alone) and Rails' request forgery protection only applies to non-GET verbs. Consequence is twofold: (1) any third-party page can CSRF a logged-in Discourse user into being silently demoted from a topic via `` or a similar tag; (2) combined with the `ensure_logged_in` issue above, the action also doesn't authorise the email recipient — once the recipient logs in, whoever's session that is has their preference for that topic changed, which is the wrong user. This should be either a POST endpoint protected by CSRF token, or a GET that requires a server-signed token tied to (user, topic) — the same pattern already used by `EmailUnsubscribeKey` in Discourse.

findings.title: MessageBuilder spec does not assert that the per-topic unsubscribe URL reaches the email body
findings.body: The test was updated to pass `unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe"` to MessageBuilder, but the only body assertion in the `add_unsubscribe_link true` context still only checks for the global `user_preferences_url`. There is no expectation that the supplied `unsubscribe_url` is interpolated into the rendered `body` (or `html_part`). A regression where the new `%{unsubscribe_url}` placeholder is silently dropped (e.g. a missing I18n interpolation variable, or a typo in the gsub) would not be caught. Add an assertion such as `expect(message_with_unsubscribe.body).to match("/t/1234/unsubscribe")` and one for `html_part` too.

findings.title: New TopicsController#unsubscribe action has no controller spec
findings.body: The `unsubscribe` action at lines 98-116 introduces nontrivial behaviour — slug-aware 301 redirect to `topic.unsubscribe_url`, conditional demotion of `TopicUser.notification_level` between `:regular` and `:muted`, mutation via direct `find_by` + `save!` rather than `TopicUser.change` (so it bypasses the `MessageBus` publish and `notifications_changed_at`/`notifications_reason_id` updates other code paths rely on), and rendering `show` via `perform_show_response` — yet the PR adds no controller request spec. The two bugs above (`ensure_logged_in` and the nil `tu` dereference) would both be caught by even a basic logged-in request spec.

findings.title: unsubscribe_link translation silently requires unsubscribe_url with no contract enforcement
findings.body: The `unsubscribe_link` translation was rewritten to interpolate `%{unsubscribe_url}` (line 1855), but `Email::MessageBuilder` (lib/email/message_builder.rb) does not enforce that the key is present in `template_args` — it just calls `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` and `gsub`s the result. Any caller that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without also passing `unsubscribe_url` will produce an email whose "click here" link has an empty `href` or a literal `%{unsubscribe_url}` placeholder. Today only `UserNotifications#send_notification_email` passes the new option, but there is nothing to stop the next mailer that copies the pattern from forgetting it. Either provide a default in the translation, document the requirement next to the `add_unsubscribe_link` keyword, or have MessageBuilder raise when the key is missing.
